To give both the employee and Simtora a structured period to assess fit: the employee learns the role and culture; the manager learns the employee's strengths and needs.\n\nScope. All new regular employees. Directors and above, and employees rehired within 12 months into the same role, may be exempted in writing by HR.\n\nPolicy\n\nThe introductory period is 90 calendar days from the start date.\n\nThe introductory period does not guarantee employment for any length of time and does not change at-will status. Simtora may end employment at any time, before or after the period ends. Completing the period does not create a contract.\n\nEmployees on introductory status accrue PTO and sick leave from day one, but may use accrued PTO only after 30 days of employment unless the manager approves earlier (sick and safe leave may be used as permitted by law, from the date state law allows). Medical and other benefits begin per plan terms.\n\nEmployees on introductory status are covered by every policy in this manual, including anti-discrimination, anti-harassment and anti-retaliation rules.\n\nReview process\n\n1. Days 1–14: manager sets written objectives and explains expectations.\n2. Day 30 and 60: check-in conversations are documented.\n3. Day 75: the manager completes the Probation Review Form (Appendix C) and discusses it with the employee; the employee may add comments. The Department Head countersigns and HR reviews.\n4. Day 90: HR confirms one of three outcomes: Confirmed – introductory period successfully completed. Extended – once, for up to 30 days, where specific and documented improvement is needed. The extension letter states the goals and the review date. An extension may also be used to cover a long absence during the period. Not confirmed – employment ends. This decision is made before the period expires, is reviewed by HR, and is communicated in person where possible.\n\nWhat we look at\n\nKnowledge, skills and deliverables for the role.\n\nQuality and reliability of work, including engineering practices where relevant. Collaboration with teammates and partners; communication.\n\nAdaptability and learning speed.\n\nAdherence to Simtora values, security practices and policies.\n\nHR checks that the employee received the resources, supervision and clear expectations needed to succeed before any \"not confirmed\" decision.", "jurisdiction": "US", "department": "HR", "owner": "Chief People Officer (Head of HR)", "scores": {"bm25_rank": 16, "vector_rank": 10, "rrf": 0.02218, "score": 0.02218, "added_as": null, "part": 0}}, {"n": 8, "chunk_id": "9fa079b8-da3d-4be5-8167-8a7852ade4ef", "document_id": "5f44eaa6-39d6-4042-8553-cde86bc5bb52", "doc_code": "SIM-HR-103", "title": "France HR Manual (Paris)", "section_path": ["Part 9 – Performance, Discipline and Separation", "9.1 Performance and Career Interviews"], "section_number": "9.1", "section_title": "Performance and Career Interviews", "page_start": 29, "page_end": 29, "content_type": "prose", "text": "9.1 Performance and Career Interviews\n\nSIM-HR-001 2.1 applies: objectives, one-to-ones, mid-year and annual review, calibration.
